newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: POLL-Consumer spending to lift SM H1 net.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Consumer spending to lift SM H1 net.

text.p: The income of mall developer SM Prime Holdings Inc could rise by more than 30 percent in the first half of this year, benefiting from retail growth driven by a rising number of affluent Filipinos, analysts said.
A Reuters poll completed on Tuesday showed that SM Prime's income could rise by an average 32.76 percent to 1.094 billion pesos ($41 million) from 824 million a year-ago.

Full-year growth was estimated at 26.23 percent to an average of 2.416 billion pesos, slightly higher than the company's own projection of 2.4 billion. The company posted a 1.914 billion peso net income last year.
"SM Prime tends to be conservative in its estimates. They've always outdone their own projections," said Iva Gutierrez, an analyst at DBP-Daiwa Securities (Philippines) Inc.
Abacus Securities research head Dennis Rayala projected a 21 percent increase in its revenue due to a 10 percent escalation in rental fees and higher sales reported by its tenants.
"SM malls are really drawing in the crowd," Rayala said, adding that shopping had become the favourite leisure activity of Filipinos.
Besides fixed rental fees based on the floor area, SM Prime also charges three to five percent of its tenants' gross sales.
The sales percentage tax accounted for 75 to 80 percent of its total revenues last year.
Anscor-Hagedorn Securities research head Noel Reyes said SM malls were direct beneficiaries of the rising disposable income of Filipinos.
"More and more people are going to the malls. It's becoming part of our culture," Reyes said.

Michelle Benedicto, an analyst at Asian Capital Equities, said SM malls catered to all income groups, unlike rivals Ayala Land Inc, which targeted high-class shoppers, and Ever Gotesco Resources & Holdings Inc and Uniwide Holdings Inc, which aimed for lower-income groups.
This year, SM expanded its gross floor area by 27,000 square metres, taking its total to 1.09 million square metres spread across five malls -- four in Manila and one in central Cebu city.
The expansion this year would further boost its first-half income, Reyes said.
It is set to open one mall in the industrial Cavite province in late July and another in suburban Quezon city in October, which will increase its mall space by a further 20 percent.
The two new malls might not contribute much to the company's bottom line this year, but were expected to be major contributors in the coming years.
The company plans to open two new malls every year for the next five years.
DBP-Daiwa's Gutierrez said the company's land bank was strategically located to serve the fast-growing population.
"The malls are strategically located. It won't face any problem of possible glut," she added.

SM Prime is majority owned by Henry Sy, one of the wealthiest Chinese-Filipino tycoons. He built his fortune by selling shoes in a small store called ShoeMart (SM) in downtown Manila that later became a household name for shoes.
